headline: Roosevelt died in April, Germany surrendered in May, and two cities were destroyed by single bombs in August
texture: Roosevelt died on April 12 and Harry Truman became president the same day, having been told almost nothing about the bomb. Hitler took residence in the Fuhrerbunker in January, dismissed Himmler from command in March, and killed himself there with Eva Braun. Germany's final instrument of surrender was signed shortly before midnight on May 8, which was already May 9 in Moscow.

The Enola Gay dropped a uranium bomb on Hiroshima on August 6 and Bockscar dropped a plutonium bomb on Nagasaki three days later. Hirohito announced the surrender by radio broadcast on August 15, the first time most Japanese had heard his voice. The final instrument was signed on September 2. The Allied leaders had met at Yalta in February and at Potsdam from July 17.

Founding negotiations for the United Nations opened in San Francisco on April 25. The biggest picture of the year was a sequel to the biggest picture of the year before, both of them Crosby as the same priest. Best Picture went instead to The Lost Weekend, about a writer on a four-day bender. Anne Frank died of typhus at Bergen-Belsen in the early part of the year, Mussolini was killed in April, and Bela Bartok died in New York.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.value: Franklin D. Roosevelt (D) until April 12, then Harry S. Truman (D)

pol.roosevelt_dies.label: Roosevelt dies in office
pol.roosevelt_dies.value: Vice President Harry Truman became the 33rd president the same day
pol.roosevelt_dies.detail: Roosevelt had been elected four times and died three months into the fourth term.

world.ve_day.label: Victory in Europe
world.ve_day.value: The final German instrument of surrender was signed shortly before midnight, already May 9 in Moscow
world.ve_day.detail: Canadian troops moved into Amsterdam as German forces there surrendered.

world.hitler_death.label: Hitler kills himself
world.hitler_death.value: Died in the Fuhrerbunker in Berlin with Eva Braun
world.hitler_death.detail: He had moved into the bunker on January 16, appointed Himmler to an army command on January 25 and dismissed him on March 20, and issued the Nero Decree ordering the destruction of German infrastructure.

world.hiroshima.label: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
world.hiroshima.value: A US B-29, the Enola Gay, dropped a uranium bomb on the city

world.nagasaki.label: Atomic bombing of Nagasaki
world.nagasaki.value: A US B-29, Bockscar, dropped a plutonium bomb three days after Hiroshima

world.japan_surrender.label: Japan surrenders
world.japan_surrender.value: Hirohito announced the unconditional surrender by radio on August 15, and the final instrument was signed on September 2
world.japan_surrender.detail: General Tomoyuki Yamashita surrendered to Philippine and American forces the same day the instrument was accepted.

world.yalta.label: Yalta Conference
world.yalta.value: The Allied leaders met to decide postwar Europe and to establish the United Nations

world.potsdam.label: Potsdam Conference
world.potsdam.value: The three main Allied leaders met from July 17 to August 2

world.united_nations.label: United Nations negotiated
world.united_nations.value: Founding negotiations opened in San Francisco

world.setif.label: Setif and Guelma massacre
world.setif.value: Thousands died in Algeria as French troops and settlers put down protests, beginning on the day Europe celebrated

Leave Her to Heaven, $5,550,000, 20th Century Fox

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre. Attendance was at its historic high, and the newsreels that year carried the camps and then the bomb.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: Relief arriving twice, in May and again in August, on top of a president's funeral and a weapon nobody outside a few thousand people had known existed.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31. It rose in October.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: Detroit Tigers beat the Chicago Cubs

deaths.roosevelt.label: Franklin D. Roosevelt
deaths.roosevelt.detail: 32nd president of the United States, in his fourth term.

deaths.anne_frank.label: Anne Frank
deaths.anne_frank.value: Died of typhus at Bergen-Belsen in February or March
deaths.anne_frank.detail: German-born Jewish diarist. The source gives the month as uncertain.

deaths.mussolini.detail: Italian politician and journalist, prime minister and Duce.

notes: Research pass July 2026. Hitler's death, Mussolini's death and Bartok's carry no date because the source lists them as undated sub-entries. Anne Frank's month is uncertain in the source and is left uncertain here. Truman being told almost nothing about the bomb, Bartok dying in New York, Brasillach being shot for collaboration, Hirohito's voice being unfamiliar to most Japanese, and 1945 attendance being a historic high are general knowledge rather than claims from the year pages.
